post.description:
**Deprecated 2026-08-05.** The client reverted to §4.1 phone + OTP, and the app no longer calls this. It is kept working, not deleted: the JWKS verification and 22 integration tests are correct, and Telegram remains the obvious cheap-verification path if it is wanted again.

Send the `id_token` the Telegram Login SDK returned; it is verified against Telegram’s JWKS with this bot’s id as the audience before any account is touched.

Registration and login are the same call - the client cannot know which one it is doing, and asking it to would create a way to probe which Telegram accounts are registered. `isNewUser` tells the client to route into role selection rather than the home screen.

A token whose `phone` scope was declined is refused while `TELEGRAM_REQUIRE_PHONE` is on: an account with no phone number cannot take part in BR-09 contact exposure, and finding that out at login is better than after building a profile.

parameters.name: x-lang
parameters.description: Interface language. Becomes the account’s stored locale when this login creates it (§3.2); change it later with PATCH /users/me/locale.

post.summary: Log in with Telegram (deprecated - use POST /auth/otp/verify)

post.description: Rotation is mandatory: the presented token is revoked and replaced. Presenting an already-used token revokes **every** session in that rotation family, so the client must single-flight refresh.
Idempotent, and deliberately public: a client whose access token has already expired must still be able to log out.

post.summary: Revoke every session for this account (§4.2)

post.description: Additive and idempotent. The new roles reach the token on the next refresh or role switch.
post.summary: Select roles at the end of registration (§2.3)

post.description: Returns a new access token carrying the requested role. The grant is verified in the database, not against the presented token’s claims.

Registration and login are one flow for a phone-only identity (§4.1). TTL, resend delay and attempt limits are server configuration (§4.2). Rate limited per phone and per IP; a 429 carries `Retry-After`.

**No SMS is sent yet** - no provider is connected. Set `OTP_STATIC_CODE` to issue a fixed code, and `OTP_ECHO_IN_RESPONSE` to return it as `devCode`. Both are refused when `NODE_ENV=production`.
post.summary: Send a login or registration code

post.description: Identical to send: the resend delay is enforced there, and a new code supersedes the previous one so only one is ever valid.

Creates the account when the phone is new. `isNewUser` tells the client to route into role selection rather than the home screen.

Verifying a code is what makes the phone number verified, so an account reaching a session through this route always satisfies **BR-01**.
post.summary: Verify a code and open a session

get.description: Identity, locale, account status and granted roles. Roles come from the database rather than the token, so a role granted since the token was issued is visible here before the next refresh.

patch.description: Stored on the account, so the choice follows the user to every signed-in device rather than staying on the install that changed it.

post.description: Moves the account to `deletion_requested` and writes a status-history row. No purge date is returned: the retention period is still an open client question.

get.description: One request tells a cold client exactly what it needs to refetch. Locale-independent, so it is safe to cache across a language change.

parameters.name: x-lang
parameters.description: uz-Latn | uz-Cyrl | ru | en. The aliases `uz` and `oz` are accepted; the response always echoes the canonical form. Unknown values fall back to uz-Latn rather than failing the request.

get.description: For rendering historical records that reference values the client never cached. Not a picker source - use `GET /dictionaries/{type}` for that.

parameters.name: x-lang
parameters.description: uz-Latn | uz-Cyrl | ru | en. The aliases `uz` and `oz` are accepted; the response always echoes the canonical form. Unknown values fall back to uz-Latn rather than failing the request.

parameters.name: ids
parameters.description: Comma-separated ids. Resolves inactive and merged items too, which is the point: a historical record must render a label, never a code.

get.summary: Resolve specific ids, including inactive and merged ones

get.description: Labels are display-only. Every filter and every write body carries ids (BR-13) - if a label ever needs to travel client → server, the contract is wrong.

parameters.name: x-lang
parameters.description: uz-Latn | uz-Cyrl | ru | en. The aliases `uz` and `oz` are accepted; the response always echoes the canonical form. Unknown values fall back to uz-Latn rather than failing the request.

parameters.name: type
parameters.description: occupation | skill | industry | region | language | employment_type | work_format | shift | attribute | skill_level | language_level | education_level | payment_period | file_purpose

parameters.name: since
parameters.description: Return only what changed after this revision. Omit for the full set. Take the value from the previous response’s `version`, never from a local counter.

304.description: The client’s `If-None-Match` matches the current version.

get.summary: Items of one dictionary type, in full or as a delta

get.description: Core and category sections together, so every code in `requiredForSearchable` resolves to a field the client can focus. Attachments are outside the field union (§4.5) and carry their own rules.

parameters.name: x-lang
parameters.description: Locale for every `label` in the response. Canonical form is echoed back.

parameters.name: category
parameters.description: Work category the form is for. Drives which fields exist and which are required (§5.2) - a candidate’s category comes from their primary occupation and is reported on the profile.

304.description: The client’s `If-None-Match` matches the current version.

get.summary: The candidate profile form for one work category

get.description: The same mechanism as the candidate profile, deliberately: the client renders both with one form engine, and the server validates both against these declarations. `requiredForSearchable` here means "required before the vacancy may be submitted for publication".

parameters.name: x-lang
parameters.description: Locale for every `label` in the response. Canonical form is echoed back.

parameters.name: category
parameters.description: Work category the form is for. Drives which fields exist and which are required (§5.2) - a candidate’s category comes from their primary occupation and is reported on the profile.

304.description: The client’s `If-None-Match` matches the current version.

get.summary: The vacancy form for one work category

get.description: Always succeeds for a candidate: before the first save every field is present and empty and `isStarted` is false, so the form has one code path. `fields` is keyed by the codes of `GET /schemas/candidate-profile` and is shaped exactly as `PATCH` accepts.

patch.description: Partial by field code. The server re-validates against the same schema the client rendered (§4.2), so a stale client schema produces a clean 422 and never a corrupt row. Completeness and the derived category are recomputed from what was stored, in the same transaction.

422.description: `errors[]` carries one entry per rejected field: `code` is the schema field code, `rule` the rule that rejected it (§4.6).

put.description: Its own route rather than a schema field, for two reasons: §4.2’s `kind` union has no `enum` member, and this is the one write that must **not** refresh `lastMeaningfulUpdateAt` (§5.3) - a privacy toggle cannot be used to make a stale profile look maintained. Allowed while incomplete: BR-02 gates the effect, not the setting.

get.description: Current roles first, then most recent. Only `roleTitle` and `startedOn` are required: §5.1 asks for a simplified entry for informal or seasonal work, where there is often no employer to name.

put.description: A full replacement rather than a patch: the record is small and a bespoke editor submits the whole form, so a partial write would only add a way for the two to disagree.

get.description: Optional for the work categories where §5.1 says it is not relevant - which is why no category makes it required for searchability.
CV, photo, certificates and evidence, newest first. `downloadPath` is a path on this API - there is no storage URL to leak (§11.1).

post.description: The purpose must be one the category’s schema declares. Uploading past a purpose’s `maxCount` retires the oldest file of that purpose, which is how §5.4’s "replace" works: the new file is stored first, so a failed upload never leaves the candidate without a CV.
post.summary: Upload or replace a profile file

delete.description: The metadata row is marked deleted, which is what makes the bytes unreachable. Nothing is purged: BR-14’s retention period is still open.

get.description: A 404 before the first `PUT`, unlike the candidate profile: `type` decides which fields exist, so there is no neutral empty employer to render.

put.description: A full replacement rather than a patch: the form is one screen per §6.1 and submits whole. `type` is fixed after creation. Completeness is recomputed in the same transaction, because BR-03 reads it on every vacancy submission.
put.summary: Create or replace the employer profile

get.description: `requiredEvidence` is served rather than hardcoded: which documents each employer type must provide is still an open client decision (§6.1, "if required by policy"), so the answer arrives as data.

post.description: Requires a complete profile and every document `requiredEvidence` marks required, each owned by the caller. Writes a BR-08 history row. **While the admin module is out of scope, `EMPLOYER_VERIFICATION_ENABLED` is off and this approves immediately** - recorded with a null actor and an `auto_verified_no_reviewer` reason, so the history never claims a person reviewed it.

get.description: Each item’s `text` is rendered in this request’s language, so switching language reads the whole history in the new one. Branch on `event` and follow `targetType`/`targetId` rather than parsing the sentence.

parameters.name: unreadOnly
parameters.description: Only what has not been read yet.

get.description: One indexed count over a partial index, because this is polled far more often than the list is opened.

Every category, including the one that cannot be switched off — flagged with `canDisable: false` so the screen can grey it out. A user who cannot find "account notices" in the list will assume they are off.

put.description: A disabled category stores nothing at all — not a hidden row — so the badge cannot count notifications the user asked not to receive. `account` is refused: §9.2 keeps security and account notices enabled, and a CHECK constraint refuses the row too.
put.summary: Switch a category on or off (§9.2)

post.description: Idempotent, and re-registering a token that belonged to another account **moves** it: a token identifies an app installation, not a person, and phones in this market are handed on. Call it after every SDK token refresh.

delete.description: Sign-out for one device. Deleted rather than kept: it is a decision.

post.description: BR-03 is checked here as well as at submit, so an employer who cannot publish finds out before filling in the form.

get.description: Includes closed ones: BR-11 removes a closed vacancy from discovery and keeps it in the employer’s history.

404.description: `vacancy.not_found` — also the answer for another employer’s vacancy, because confirming that an id exists is information we do not owe (§11.1).

patch.description: Partial by field code, re-validated server-side against the same schema the client rendered (§4.2). Editing a rejected vacancy returns it to `draft`; changing an age or gender restriction on a live one sends it back for review (BR-12).

post.description: Requires a verified employer (BR-03), every required field for the category, a deadline that has not passed, and — for any age or gender restriction — a justification the enumerated list supports (BR-12). **While `MODERATION_ENABLED` is off an ordinary vacancy is published immediately**, recorded with a null actor and an `auto_approved_no_moderator` reason. A vacancy carrying a BR-12 restriction still goes to review regardless, because BR-12 requires it — which means it cannot publish until the admin module (M10) exists.

422.description: One `required` violation per unfilled field, so each can be focused.

put.description: Closing is terminal (BR-11): the vacancy leaves discovery and stays in history. Every change writes a BR-08 audit row.

post.description: The administrator side of §6.4. The queue that lists what is waiting is M10; this is the decision itself, kept with the transition rules and their audit rows rather than duplicated in the admin module. A rejection requires a reason.
post.summary: Approve or reject a submitted vacancy (BR-04)

get.description: Rule-based on the candidate’s own occupations, region and category — not a model (ARCHITECTURE.md §12 defers that). A candidate with no profile gets the recent feed rather than an empty one.

get.description: Includes the employer’s verification status and the structured requirements. Visible only while the vacancy is (BR-04, BR-11).

put.description: Idempotent: saving twice is saving once.

post.description: Filed as a complaint for M10’s review queue. One open report per person per vacancy — tapping Report twice is not two complaints.

BR-06, BR-07 and BR-08 are enforced in one transaction: the vacancy is read `FOR SHARE` so it cannot close underneath the insert, the partial unique index is what stops a concurrent double-tap, and the `submitted` history row is written with the application.

parameters.name: Idempotency-Key
parameters.description: Optional. A retry with the same key and the same body returns the original application instead of failing (§12.4); a different body under the same key is a 409. Separate from BR-07, which prevents the duplicate itself.

409.description: `application.already_applied` (BR-07) or `application.vacancy_closed` (BR-06, and BR-04/BR-11 — from the candidate’s side they are one fact).

get.summary: Applications to one of the caller’s vacancies (§6.5)
The caller’s applications and their stages (§5.6)

post.description: Allowed up to an accepted offer, which `hired` being terminal expresses. Frees the BR-07 slot, so the candidate may apply again later.

get.summary: Hires against the requirement, and a stage breakdown (§6.5)

put.description: Forward moves may skip a stage — real hiring does — but never go backwards: a candidate told they were shortlisted and then returned to `viewed` has been told something false. `hired` increments the vacancy’s counter in the same transaction (§6.5).
put.summary: Move an application through the stages (§8.1, §6.5)

get.description: The candidate’s profile and "authorized CV". `phone` is present only where the candidate’s privacy settings **and** a hiring interaction both allow it, and `exposureReason` says which rule decided. Every call is logged (§11.1).
get.summary: The applicant, as much of them as BR-09 allows (§6.5)

get.description: §6.5’s "authorized CV". BR-09 is re-evaluated on every download rather than trusted from the listing call, because a client may hold a path from a moment when the interaction still existed — so a candidate who withdraws stops the download working. Streamed through this API after the check; there is no storage URL to leak (§11.1). Every download is logged.

404.description: `file.not_found` — unknown, not this candidate’s, or BR-09 does not allow it. One code for all three: which it was is not information we owe.

post.description: **Not visible to the candidate.** No candidate-facing read returns these.

get.description: Every status change with its time and actor role. Readable by the candidate who applied and by the employer who owns the vacancy - the same trail both sides are held to.

post.description: Verified employers only. Every result is a searchable, complete profile (BR-02), and **no card carries a phone number or a CV** (§11.1) — a card is not a hiring interaction, so BR-09 never opens for one. `matchScore` is the weighted share of the filters each candidate satisfies, and `matchBreakdown` says which groups made it up.

403.description: `employer.profile_incomplete` or `employer.not_verified` (§7, BR-03); `search.restriction_not_justified` for an unjustified age or gender filter (BR-12); `search.occupation_required` when occupation experience is filtered without an occupation.

post.description: Capped at 200. `isExact: false` means "200+", which is the honest answer to a filter set matching thousands — §7.2 asks for this "where technically reasonable", and an exact count of a huge set is the part that is not.
post.summary: How many candidates match, before opening the list (§7.2)

get.description: Mandatory requirements become filters; **preferred ones deliberately do not** — a preference that excluded candidates would not be a preference, and the match score rewards them instead. Mandatory skills prefill as match-all, which may match nobody: that is what §7.2’s count is for. BR-12 restrictions come across with the justification the vacancy already carries.
get.summary: The vacancy’s requirements as an editable filter set (UAT-06)

get.description: Readable while the candidate is searchable, or whenever a hiring interaction exists — an applicant stays readable after hiding their profile. `phone` and the files are present only where BR-09 allows, and `exposureReason` says which rule decided. Every call is logged (§11.1).

404.description: `candidate.profile_not_found` — unknown, or not findable and no interaction.

get.summary: §7.3’s "View profile", as much of it as BR-09 allows

get.description: The one candidate file an employer may read without a hiring interaction, and it is narrow on purpose: only the file whose purpose is `photo`, only for a searchable profile, only for a verified employer. A photo uploaded to be found by is not §5.4’s authorized CV; every other file still needs BR-09.

The same cards, and **still behind BR-02’s gate**: a candidate who hides their profile leaves every employer’s saved list. Otherwise "hide me from search" would be defeated by whoever saved them first. The save itself survives, so they return if they choose to.

put.description: Idempotent: saving twice is saving once.
Saves the candidate if they were not saved yet — the note is about the save. **Never visible to the candidate**, and no candidate-facing read touches the table.
Not conditional on having saved them: §7.3 describes the flow a user takes, and failing a two-tap action for a rule nobody depends on would be noise.
put.summary: Add a candidate to this vacancy’s shortlist (§7.3)

delete.summary: Remove a candidate from a shortlist

post.description: Verified employers only (BR-03), and only a **search-visible** candidate — an employer cannot invite somebody they could not have found, which is BR-02’s gate again. A vacancy invitation needs an **active** vacancy, checked with the same definition of "open" the apply route uses (BR-06), so an invitation cannot advertise something that would refuse the application. One open invitation per candidate per vacancy; answering frees the slot.

parameters.name: Idempotency-Key
parameters.description: Optional. A retry with the same key and the same body returns the original invitation instead of a conflict (§12.4) — which is what makes a lost response safe. A different body under the same key is a 409.

post.summary: Invite a candidate to a vacancy, or generally (§8.2)

get.description: §7.4 tracks "invited, accepted, interviewed and hired counts against the target". The first two are here; the last two are application stages and come from `/vacancies/{id}/applications/counts`.
get.summary: Invitations for one vacancy, by status (§7.4)

get.description: The invitation’s counterpart to the application-scoped download, and separate for the same reason: the entitlement comes from the interaction, so the route that serves the bytes has to be the one that can see it. BR-09 is re-evaluated per download rather than trusted from a path the client is holding. Every download is logged (§11.1).

404.description: `file.not_found` — unknown, not this candidate’s, the invitation is not yours, or it has not been accepted. One code for all of them.

get.summary: Download a file of a candidate who accepted (§8.2, BR-09)

get.description: Deliberately **not** filtered by the vacancy’s visibility: an invitation to a vacancy that has since closed still has to be readable, for the same reason a saved vacancy does — a candidate needs to see what became of something addressed to them.

post.description: The candidate’s alone. `details_requested` is a question rather than an ending — accepting or declining afterwards is allowed, asking twice is not. Acceptance is what opens BR-09’s second interaction, so it reveals the contact details this employer was previously refused.

get.summary: One invitation, for either side of it

get.description: Every status change with its time and actor role, readable by both sides — the same trail both are held to.

post.description: Requires a **permitted hiring interaction** — a live application or an accepted invitation. The same question BR-09 asks, from the same service, so an employer who may see a phone number and one who may send a message are the same employer. Idempotent: there is only ever one thread between two people.
post.summary: Open the conversation with someone, or return the existing one (§9.1)

get.summary: The caller’s conversations, most recently active first

get.description: Readable whether or not sending is: §9.1 keeps closed and blocked interactions in history. Scroll back with `before`.

parameters.name: before
parameters.description: Messages older than this instant — the cursor for scrolling back.

get.summary: A page of the thread, newest first (§9.1)

post.description: The gate is re-asked here rather than trusted from when the conversation opened: an interaction can end while a client holds the screen, and a withdrawal or a declined invitation turns the thread into history mid-conversation. An attachment must be a file the sender owns.

parameters.name: Idempotency-Key
parameters.description: Optional. A retry with the same key and body returns the original message instead of sending a second one (§12.4).

409.description: `chat.read_only` — the hiring interaction has ended (§9.1). The thread stays readable.

put.description: Read state is one timestamp per participant, so this is idempotent and cheap. The other side sees it as `isReadByRecipient` on the messages they sent.
put.summary: Mark everything up to now as read (§9.1)

post.description: Read-only for **both** sides while it stands, whoever set it: a block that let the blocker keep writing would be a mute. The messages stay readable, because §9.1 keeps blocked interactions in history and a moderator needs them.
Filed as a complaint with `target_type = "message"` — the same queue M10 reviews vacancy reports through. One open report per person per message.

get.description: The third entitlement-bearing download route, and the same rule as the other two: the entitlement comes from the conversation, so the route that serves the bytes is the one that can see it. `/files/{id}/content` stays owner-only.

post.description: Moves the application to §8.1’s `interview` stage **in the same transaction**, with its BR-08 history row: the stage table says the candidate is told "date, time, type and location/link" when that stage is set, and that is this. An application already at or past the stage is left where it is; a terminal one is refused.

409.description: `application.final` — a withdrawn, rejected or hired application.

422.description: `interview.detail_required` against `location` or `meetingLink` — §8.3’s conditional requirement, which a CHECK constraint enforces underneath.

get.summary: One application’s interviews, for either side

put.description: A full replacement, not a patch: the type decides which of `location` and `meetingLink` may exist, so a partial update could leave a phone interview holding the address of the in-person one it used to be. **Always resets the candidate’s answer** — a new time has not been confirmed, whatever was said about the old one.

post.description: Not one of §8.3’s statuses, and here because the alternative is a stale interview nobody can retract — an employer whose plans change would otherwise have to reschedule to a fiction. Terminal.

get.description: Not in §8.3, which describes one interview — but a candidate with four applications needs one list of where to be and when. Cancelled ones are left out.
get.summary: The caller’s interviews across every application

post.description: The candidate’s alone. `confirmed` is **not** terminal: a candidate who confirms and then finds a clash must be able to say so. Saying the same thing twice is refused, because a second identical history row records that nothing happened.

get.description: Every status change with its time and actor role, readable by both sides — the same trail both are held to.

Totals and queue lengths in one request. The period counts are "newly registered" and "active vacancies and applications for the selected period"; a queue length is current state, because what matters about a queue is how long it is now. `to` is inclusive. Defaults to the last 30 days.

parameters.name: from
parameters.description: Start of §10.1’s "selected period", inclusive. Defaults to 30 days ago.

parameters.name: to
parameters.description: End of the period, **inclusive**. Defaults to today.

get.description: Oldest submission first — a queue that is not FIFO is a queue somebody waits in. Each item carries its evidence as paths on this API; there is no storage URL to hand out (ARCHITECTURE.md §9).

post.description: M4 holds the transitions, the mandatory reason and the BR-08 history row; this route supplies the administrator and the audit entry. Approving is what makes BR-03 pass for that employer, so it unblocks their vacancies and invitations.

get.description: The file must belong to a submission of that employer: an administrator may read evidence, not any file whose id they can name. Every download is logged, because §11.1 requires access to protected data to be.
get.summary: Download a piece of verification evidence (§10.2, §11.1)

get.description: Oldest first, and each item says whether it carries a BR-12 age or gender restriction — §10.2 requires those to be reviewed, and a restricted vacancy cannot publish any other way.

get.summary: The vacancy, its requirements and its restriction (§10.2)

post.description: M5 holds the transitions and the mandatory rejection reason. Approving a BR-12 restricted vacancy is the **only** way it can publish — that is the point of making review part of the rule rather than an optimisation.
post.summary: Approve or reject a vacancy (§10.2, BR-04, BR-12)

put.description: For a vacancy that is already published — a complaint upheld, a policy breach. Same transition table and BR-08 history row as the employer’s own status change; only the actor and the missing ownership check differ.
put.summary: Pause or remove a live vacancy (§10.2)

get.description: Over all four target kinds — users, vacancies, messages and profiles — from the one generic table M6 created, so there is one queue rather than four.

parameters.name: targetType
parameters.description: §10.2 reviews reported users, vacancies, messages and profiles.

get.description: The target is resolved per kind — the message that was reported, the vacancy’s title, the person’s name and account state. Deliberately small: this is a review screen, and the full record is one link away.
get.summary: One complaint, with enough of its target to judge it (§10.2)

post.description: The resolution is mandatory, and the audit row is written **in the same transaction** — nothing else records a complaint review, so unlike a verification decision there is no BR-08 row standing behind it.

409.description: `complaint.not_open` — unknown, or somebody reviewed it first.

get.description: By partial phone, name, role, status or registration date. The name is matched against a candidate’s profile, an individual employer’s own name and a company’s public or legal name. Every search is logged (§11.1).

parameters.name: phone
parameters.description: A partial phone number (§10.4).

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: Matched against a candidate’s name, an individual employer’s own name and a company’s public or legal name — an administrator should not have to know which kind of account it is.

get.description: BR-08’s account status trail and the complaints filed about them — the two halves of §10.4’s "relevant moderation history".
get.summary: One user, with their moderation history (§10.4)

post.description: Changes no account status: the audit row **is** the record, which is the clearest answer to why an audit log exists when six tables already record status changes. M9 adds the notification that tells them.

put.description: A mandatory reason, an `account_status_history` row (BR-08) and an audit row, in one transaction. `restrictedUntil` makes a restriction temporary — BR-10’s guard lifts it when the date passes. An administrator cannot target themselves, because no route would undo it.

409.description: `admin.status_unchanged` — already in that state, or awaiting deletion, which BR-14 owns.

put.summary: Restrict, block or unblock a user (§10.4, UAT-14)

post.description: Inactive unless you say otherwise, because an item with no labels must not reach a picker. Activation is refused by the database while any of the four labels is missing (§3.2).

put.description: Any subset. Every write bumps the global dictionary revision through a trigger, so clients learn of the change through the delta they already poll.
put.summary: Edit an item’s metadata or labels (§10.3)

put.description: Deactivating keeps it resolvable for historical records — it only leaves the pickers. **Nothing is ever hard-deleted** (BR-13).

422.description: Activation with a missing locale fails on the deferrable constraint that derives the required set from the `locale_code` enum.

post.description: The item in the path loses: it is deactivated and points at the survivor, so every profile and vacancy that referenced it still resolves through `GET /dictionaries/items?ids=`. Nothing is rewritten — that would be a migration disguised as an edit — and both revisions bump, so one delta carries both sides.
post.summary: Merge a duplicate into a survivor (§10.3)

get.description: "Available to authorized administrators", newest first, filterable by actor or by target. **Append-only in the database**: three statement-level triggers refuse `UPDATE`, `DELETE` and `TRUNCATE`, so immutability is a property of the table rather than of this module having no write path.

parameters.name: actorUserId
parameters.description: "What has this administrator done" (§10.4).

parameters.name: targetType
parameters.description: "What was done to this thing" — the other question asked of the log.

get.description: BR-14 defers to "the approved privacy policy", and there is not one yet. Rather than leave the periods undefined, the platform declares them here with a **provenance** tag on each: `provisional` means an engineer chose the number and no lawyer has seen it, `required` means another rule fixes it. The answer from the client is an edit to one table in the source, not a milestone.

A preview, and the reason there is no scheduler behind any of this: while the periods are provisional, an administrator looks at what is due before anything is erased. `action` is `anonymize` for an account that is the actor on an audit row - §10.4 will not let that row lose who acted, so the person is erased and the id survives.

post.description: Erases everything `due` listed, one account per transaction, and writes a `user.purged` audit row for each. An account that cannot be purged is reported in `failed` rather than rolling back the rest. **Irreversible** - the only recovery is a restore from docs/BACKUP.md.
Type and size are validated against the file’s actual content, not its name. The response carries a path on this API, never a storage URL.

parameters.name: purpose
parameters.description: Restrict to one `file_purpose` code.

get.description: Streamed through this API after an ownership check. `Content-Disposition` is `attachment` and `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff` is set, so an uploaded document can never be rendered as a page in the caller’s origin.

delete.description: The metadata row is marked deleted, which is what makes the file unreachable. Nothing is purged: BR-14’s retention period is still open.

get.description: Always returns 200 when the process is serving. Inspect the `status` and `database` fields to tell healthy from degraded.

idToken.description: The `id_token` returned by the Telegram Login SDK. A JWT signed by `https://oauth.telegram.org`, verified server-side against Telegram’s JWKS with this bot’s id as the audience. Never send the raw OAuth `code` here - the SDK completes that exchange.

activeRole.description: Null when the account holds several roles and has not chosen one, or holds none yet. The client must call /auth/active-role before acting.

isNewUser.description: True when this verification created the account.

isCurrent.description: True for the session this request authenticated with.

roles.description: One account may hold several roles (§2.3). `admin` is granted by an administrator, never self-assigned.

purpose.description: Registration and login are the same flow for a phone-only identity; the server decides which happened. Pass `phone_change` only from an authenticated phone-change flow.

resendAvailableAt.description: Earliest time a resend will be accepted (§4.2).

devCode.description: Development only, when OTP_ECHO_IN_RESPONSE is on. Boot refuses this flag in production.

phone.description: E.164. Returned only to the account owner (§11.1, BR-09). Null when the account signed in with Telegram and declined the `phone` scope - only possible while the server allows that.

telegramUsername.description: Telegram `@username` without the `@`, when the account is linked to Telegram. User-changeable, so never an identity - support and display only.

status.description: A restricted or blocked account is refused every mutation (BR-10); the client reads this to explain why rather than guessing from a 403.

locale.description: Canonical BCP-47 code (docs/API_CONTRACTS.md §1). The house aliases `uz`/`oz` are accepted on the `x-lang` header, not here: this value is persisted, so it is stored in exactly one form.

purgeAfter.description: Retention period is not yet defined (BR-14 defers to the approved privacy policy), so no purge date is returned yet.

count.description: Active items only - what a picker would show.

version.description: Newest revision anywhere in the dictionaries.

schemas.description: Ten entries: five §2.1 categories × two targets. Versions are locale-independent, so a label edit in any locale bumps all four.

code.description: Stable machine code. Diagnostics and deep links only - never displayed to a user (§3.2).

label.description: Resolved for the request locale via the §3.2 fallback chain.

category.description: Set on occupations and work types (§2.1); null elsewhere.

group.description: Second grouping, used by `attribute` items only (§6.3 additional structured requirements) and referenced by a schema field’s `group`.

parentId.description: Parent item, e.g. the region a district belongs to.

rank.description: Non-null only on the ordered scales (`skill_level`, `language_level`), where it is the value a “≥ C1” comparison uses (§7.4).

mergedIntoId.description: The surviving item when this one was merged away (§10.3).

reason.description: Drop the id from pickers. It still resolves forever through `GET /dictionaries/items`.

locale.description: Canonical form of the resolved locale. Key the client cache off this, not off the value sent in `x-lang` (docs/API_CONTRACTS.md §1).

version.description: Pass back as `since` on the next request.

isFull.description: True when this response is the whole set.

kind.description: Closed union of 13 members (§4.2). An unknown value must be skipped and logged, never crash the form - that is what lets the server add a field type without a lockstep app release.

required.description: Required before the profile may become searchable (BR-02), for this category only.

dictionaryType.description: Dictionary type to load options from, for the `dictionary_*` kinds.

group.description: `attribute` items only: offer just this `group` (§3.4) - `licence`, `transport`, `tools` or `readiness`.

parentFieldCode.description: Restrict the options to the children of the item chosen in this field - a district within the selected region.

source.description: Where the value is stored server-side. Informational: the client renders both the same way (§4.1).

editor.description: `bespoke` hands the section to a purpose-built widget; `fields` is then empty and `endpoint` names its sub-resource.

accept.description: Advisory mirror of the server rules; the server rejects violations regardless.

maxCount.description: Uploading beyond this supersedes the oldest file of the purpose.

schemaVersion.description: Also published in `GET /dictionaries/manifest`, so one request tells a cold client whether any schema changed.

requiredForSearchable.description: Field codes that must be filled before the profile can be searchable (BR-02). Every code resolves to a field in `sections[].fields[]`, so a completeness prompt can always focus one.

code.description: Field code, or a bespoke section’s code.

required.description: True when BR-02 blocks searchability on it. False entries are prompts, not blockers.

isStarted.description: False until the first save. Every other field is still present and empty, so the form renders identically for a new and an existing profile.

category.description: Derived from the primary occupation, and what to pass to `GET /schemas/candidate-profile`. Null until one is chosen, when only the fields common to all categories exist.

completenessPercent.description: Measured over every field of the category plus experience and education (§5.3). Stored server-side; recomputing it client-side guarantees the two disagree.

isComplete.description: Every required field is filled. BR-02’s first condition.

isSearchable.description: BR-02 in full: complete **and** visibility is `searchable`. What decides whether an employer can find this profile.

fields.description: Current values by field code, in the same shape `PATCH` accepts - read, edit one value, send it back.

lastMeaningfulUpdateAt.description: Last change to actual profile content (§5.3). A privacy toggle does not move it, so it cannot be used to look freshly maintained.

fields.description: Field codes from `GET /schemas/candidate-profile`, each carrying the value shape its `kind` declares (§4.2). Partial: only the codes present are written. `null` clears a field - requiredness gates searchability (BR-02), never the save. A list field states the whole list, so removing one entry means sending the others.

visibility.description: `searchable` - visible in employer search; `hidden` - excluded from it while the candidate can still browse and apply; `visible_after_apply` - visible only to employers whose vacancy the candidate applied to.

employerName.description: Optional, because §5.1 asks for "simplified entry for informal or seasonal work" - a seasonal worker often cannot name an employer.

roleTitle.description: The one required field: what the person did.

occupationId.description: `occupation` dictionary id, so §7.1’s "years in the selected occupation" can be computed rather than guessed from the title text.

isCurrent.description: Still working here. Mutually exclusive with `endedOn`.

graduationYear.description: An expected graduation up to ten years out is accepted; the column carries the same bound as a CHECK.

downloadPath.description: Path on this API. Bytes are proxied after an ownership check - a storage URL would carry the bot token and could never reach a client (ARCHITECTURE.md §9).

purpose.description: `file_purpose` **code** - `cv`, `photo`, `certificate` or `evidence`. The code rather than the id, so the client can upload without having resolved the dictionary first; the schema’s `attachments[]` carries both.

file.description: Validated against its actual content, not its name: extension, declared MIME type and magic bytes must agree (§12.5).

field.description: Response field name, so the client can focus it.

verificationStatus.description: The five states of §6.1, shown to the employer as-is.

verificationReason.description: The administrator’s reason for a rejection or a correction request. Human text, already in the language it was written in - not a translatable key.

completenessPercent.description: Over the fields §6.1 requires for this employer type.

isComplete.description: BR-03’s condition: an employer may not submit a vacancy or send an invitation until this is true.

canPublish.description: Both BR-03 conditions together: complete **and** verified. §7 requires this for candidate search.

type.description: Chosen once. It decides which fields apply (§6.1) and what verification asks for, so a later change would strand the other type’s answers and the evidence verification was granted against - `employer.type_immutable`.

contactPhone.description: The number a candidate should call. Deliberately separate from the login phone: the verified identity (BR-01) must not be overwritten by a business contact detail.

description.description: A company description, or for an individual employer the "short description of the requested work" of §6.1.

publicName.description: Companies: the name shown on a vacancy card, which often differs.

logoFileId.description: Companies: a stored file of purpose `logo`, uploaded via `/files`.

required.description: Whether a submission is refused without it. What each type must provide is still an open client decision (§6.1 "if required by policy"), so read this rather than hardcoding a list.

submissions.description: Newest first. Past attempts and why they were refused.

fileIds.description: Stored file ids, uploaded through `POST /files` with the purpose the verification state lists as required. Must belong to the caller.

event.description: The §9.2 event, as a stable code. Branch on this rather than on the text.

text.description: Rendered **now**, in the language of this request (`x-lang`). The row stores a message key and its parameters rather than text, so a user who switches language sees their whole history in the new one (§3.2).

canDisable.description: False for `account`. §9.2: "security and account notices remain enabled" — it is listed so the settings screen can show it greyed out rather than omitting it, because a user who cannot find it will assume it is off.

enabled.description: False switches the category off. Refused for `account` with `notification.category_not_disableable`, and a CHECK constraint refuses the row underneath.

token.description: The FCM registration token. Re-register it whenever the SDK rotates it — a token is unique across users, so registering one that belonged to another account moves it, which is what a shared or resold phone needs.

appVersion.description: For support, when a bug is version-specific.

moderationReason.description: The moderator’s reason for a rejection, as written.

fields.description: Current values by field code, in the same shape `PATCH` accepts — read, edit one value, send it back.

missingForSubmit.description: Required field codes still unfilled. `POST /submit` refuses while this is non-empty, with one 422 violation per code.

isOpenForApplications.description: BR-06 in one field: active, and either no deadline or one that has not passed. What decides whether an application is accepted.

fields.description: Field codes from `GET /schemas/vacancy`, each carrying the value shape its `kind` declares (§4.2). Partial: only the codes present are written. A list field states the whole list. Editing a rejected vacancy returns it to `draft`; editing an age or gender restriction on a live one sends it back for review (BR-12).

status.description: `paused` hides it from discovery temporarily; `active` resumes it; `closed` is terminal — BR-11 removes it from discovery and keeps it in history.

reason.description: Why it was closed. Shown in the employer’s history.

decision.description: BR-04: a vacancy is not visible until approved.

reason.description: Mandatory when rejecting — a refusal the employer cannot act on is not a decision.

name.description: A company’s public name or an individual’s own name — never the legal name, which §6.1 keeps separately because the two differ.

isVerified.description: §5.6 shows verification status on the vacancy itself.

applicationStatus.description: The caller’s own application stage for this vacancy, or null. Lets the card show Apply or the current status without a second request (§5.6).

reason.description: Why it is being reported. Free text: a candidate reporting a fake vacancy should not have to find their objection on a list. M10 reviews it.

coverNote.description: An optional short message (§5.6). Optional on purpose: a candidate applying to twenty seasonal vacancies will not write twenty letters.

rejectionReason.description: The employer’s reason, when rejected. Visible to the candidate.

status.description: §8.1’s employer-settable stages. Forward moves may skip — real hiring does — but never backwards, and `withdrawn` is the candidate’s alone.

reason.description: Shown to the candidate on a rejection (§8.1 "optional standard message"). Recorded in the BR-08 history whatever the stage.

phone.description: BR-09: present only where the candidate’s privacy settings **and** a hiring interaction both allow it. Null is a normal answer, not an error.

canViewFiles.description: Whether this employer may download the candidate’s files (BR-09, §5.4). When false, `files` is empty.

files.description: The candidate’s CV and other attachments, each with a path on this API. Empty unless `canViewFiles`.

exposureReason.description: Why the decision went the way it did — a stable code, logged with the access (§11.1) and useful when a candidate asks why an employer could not call them.

note.description: §6.5’s internal note. **Never visible to the candidate** — it lives in its own table so that reading it is a deliberate act rather than one forgotten `select` away from being exposed.

items.description: BR-08: every status change with its time and actor, oldest first.

minLevelRank.description: The rank of the lowest acceptable `language_level`. A rank rather than an id because §7.1 asks for a floor, and a floor is a comparison.

primaryOnly.description: Match the candidate’s primary occupation only.

skillsMatchMode.description: §7.1’s "match all or match any". `any` by default: a vacancy naming eight skills would otherwise match nobody, and §7.2’s count tells you before you open the list.

occupationExperienceYearsMin.description: Years in the occupations named by `occupationIds`, which this filter therefore requires — `search.occupation_required` without them.

currentOccupationIds.description: §7.1’s "current/last role", as the occupation of the current job.

educationLevelIds.description: Acceptable `education_level` ids. A set rather than a floor: the education row stores no rank, and §7.1 asks for the level rather than a minimum.

specializationIds.description: §7.1’s "specialization where relevant", as `specialization` dictionary ids — any of them matches. Ids and not text, because a substring match on prose cannot behave identically in four interface variants (§3.3, BR-13).

willingToTravel.description: §7.1’s travel readiness. Remote-work readiness is **not** here: it is a `work_format` id, so it belongs in `workFormatIds` where every selectable value lives (BR-13).

proximityDistrictId.description: Where to be near, for `sort: "proximity"` — a district id. Separate from `districtIds` on purpose: filtering by district excludes everyone else, leaving a proximity sort nothing to order. Prefilled from the vacancy’s district (UAT-06).

salaryMax.description: The employer’s ceiling: a candidate expecting more is filtered out. A candidate whose expectation is negotiable passes, for the same reason a negotiable vacancy passes a candidate’s salary floor.

salaryMin.description: The floor of the employer’s range.

availableImmediately.description: §7.1’s "immediately" — the same test against today in Asia/Tashkent.

attributeIds.description: Licence, transport, tool and readiness ids — one `attribute` type.

crewSizeMin.description: Candidates who can bring a crew of at least n.

ageMin.description: BR-12. Permitted only with `restrictionJustificationId`; every use is logged.

restrictionJustificationId.description: A `restriction_justification` id, required as soon as an age or gender filter is used, and it must be one the declaration permits for those kinds — the same rule a vacancy’s restriction is held to. `search.restriction_not_justified` otherwise.

sort.description: §7.3’s options. `proximity` is tiered — same district, then same region, then the rest — measured against the location this request filters on: there are no coordinates in this data model, so a kilometre figure would be invented. With no location filter there is nothing to be near, and the order falls through to recency.

vacancyId.description: The vacancy the search was opened from (UAT-06). Decides `isShortlisted` on each card; it does **not** re-apply the vacancy’s filters, which the client already holds and may have edited.

levelRank.description: The level’s rank, so a client can sort or compare.
The level’s rank, so a client can sort or compare.

group.description: One of `occupation`, `skills`, `languages`, `location`, `preferences`, `attributes` — the groups the filters actually asked about.

asked.description: How many items this group asked for.

matched.description: How many of them the candidate has.

experienceYears.description: Total years of history, summed from the experience rows. Overlapping jobs count twice, which is a known roughness rather than a hidden one.

photoPath.description: Path to the profile photo on this API, or null. The one candidate file a card may carry: a photo uploaded to be found by is not §5.4’s authorized CV.

note.description: §7.3’s private employer note. Never visible to the candidate.

isShortlisted.description: False unless the request named a `vacancyId`.

applicationStatus.description: The candidate’s stage on any of this employer’s vacancies, or null.

groups.description: The scoring groups this request used, with their weights and asked-for counts — the same objects each card’s breakdown is measured against. `matched` is 0 here.

isExact.description: False when the cap was hit, so the client can render "200+".

candidateUserId.description: The candidate, who must be search-visible (§8.2).

vacancyId.description: An **active** vacancy of the caller’s. Mutually exclusive with `occupationId`; the vacancy is where the occupation, place, schedule and pay come from.

occupationId.description: A general invitation’s occupation (§8.2). Mutually exclusive with `vacancyId`.

salaryIsNegotiable.description: Excludes a range, as everywhere else in this product: a negotiable figure and a stated one are different answers.

scheduleNote.description: §8.2’s schedule. Free text: a general invitation is a message, and the structured version of it is what publishing a vacancy is for.

message.description: §8.2’s contact context — what the employer wants to say.

vacancyId.description: Null for a general invitation, which carries its own details.

byStatus.description: Invitations for this vacancy by status (§7.4’s invited and accepted counts). Interviewed and hired are application stages — read them from `/vacancies/{id}/applications/counts`.

status.description: §8.2’s Accept, Decline or Request details. `details_requested` is not an ending: the candidate may still accept or decline afterwards, but may not ask twice.

note.description: The candidate’s reply. Where "Request details" puts its question, and it is kept as the reason on the BR-08 history row.

counterpartUserId.description: The other person. Which side of the conversation each of you is on follows from your active role, so a multi-role account (§2.3) can hold both kinds of thread.
The other participant, from the caller’s side.

counterpartName.description: The candidate’s name, or the employer’s public name — never a legal name.

unreadCount.description: Messages from the other side the caller has not read.

canSend.description: §9.1: false once the hiring interaction has ended or either side has blocked. The thread stays readable — it becomes history, not nothing.

blockedByMe.description: Whether it was the caller who blocked.

downloadPath.description: Where to fetch the attachment, scoped to this conversation. Never a storage URL (ARCHITECTURE.md §9), and never `/files/{id}/content`, which stays owner-only.

isReadByRecipient.description: §9.1’s read state, for messages the caller **sent**: has the other side read it? There is no `delivered` state — delivery is a property of push (M9), and a field set at the same moment as `createdAt` would be a fake answer.

body.description: The text. Optional only when the message carries an attachment.

fileId.description: An attachment the **sender owns** — a file id from their own uploads (§9.1 "approved attachments"). One per message.

reason.description: Why, for the moderator who reviews it (§9.1).
Free text: somebody reporting a message should not have to find their objection on a list. Filed as a `complaints` row for M10’s queue.

type.description: §8.3’s three types. The type decides which detail is required, and the server refuses the others: `in_person` needs `location`, `external_link` needs `meetingLink`, `phone` needs neither and permits neither.

scheduledAt.description: When, as an instant. Stored as `timestamptz` and returned with the platform offset (API_CONTRACTS §2), so "14:00" means the same moment to both sides.

meetingLink.description: `external_link` only. A plain string: §2.4 puts a built-in video engine out of scope, so this is somebody else’s meeting URL and nothing more.

status.description: §8.3’s "confirm or request another time". A candidate who confirmed may still ask for another time afterwards - plans change - but may not say the same thing twice.

note.description: The candidate’s reply. Where "request another time" says *which* time, and it is kept as the reason on the BR-08 history row.

reason.description: **Mandatory for anything but an approval** (§10.2, §6.1) — the employer has to know what to fix. `employer.verification_reason_required` otherwise.

decision.description: §10.2’s approve or reject. Approving publishes it (BR-04), which for a BR-12 restricted vacancy is the only way it can ever publish.

status.description: §10.2’s "pause, or remove a vacancy with an audit record".

reason.description: Mandatory: the employer is owed an explanation.

outcome.description: Whether the complaint led to an action.

resolution.description: What was decided and why. Mandatory: a review with no resolution is a status change nobody can account for.

reason.description: Mandatory (§10.4). A warning changes no account status, so this reason and the audit row are the entire record of it.

status.description: §10.4’s restrict, block and unblock (`active`). A blocked account is refused every mutation by BR-10’s guard, and so is a restricted one.

restrictedUntil.description: What makes §10.4’s restriction *temporary*: the guard lifts it once this passes, writing the BR-08 history row for the change. Ignored for the other two statuses.

labels.description: All four interface variants, keyed by locale. The database refuses to **activate** an item missing any of them (§3.2), so a partial set is only useful on a draft.

code.description: Stable code, unique within the type. Never shown to a user (BR-13).

category.description: §10.3’s "assign category" — occupations and work types only.

group.description: Second grouping: attribute groups, skill families.

rank.description: Ordered scales only, and uniform per type.

isActive.description: Inactive by default: a new item with no labels must not appear in a picker. Activate it once the four labels are in.

labels.description: Any subset of the four labels; the others are left as they are.

isActive.description: Activation fails with a constraint error if any of the four labels is missing — that rule is a deferrable trigger, so it holds against every write path (§3.2).

survivorId.description: The item that survives. The one in the path is deactivated and points at it through `merged_into_id`, so historical references still resolve (§10.3, BR-13).

code.description: Stable code, also used by the purge.

days.description: Days after the trigger. `null` means the data is kept indefinitely.

provenance.description: **`provisional` means no lawyer has seen this number.** BR-14 defers to an approved privacy policy that does not exist yet, so the platform states its assumption here rather than hiding it in a document.

legalBasis.description: Why the period cannot be zero, or must be finite.

provisional.description: Codes whose period is still an engineering default, not a client answer.

action.description: `anonymize` when the account is the actor on an audit row: §10.4 will not let that row lose who acted, so the person is erased and the actor id survives.

auditRows.description: Audit rows depending on this id surviving.

anonymized.description: Accounts whose identity was erased, id retained.

failed.description: Reported rather than thrown: one account that cannot be purged must not roll back the others.

file.description: The file itself. PDF, DOC, DOCX for a CV; PDF, JPG, PNG for certificates and evidence. The server checks the content, not just the extension.

purpose.description: A `file_purpose` dictionary code: cv, certificate or evidence. Codes come from `GET /dictionaries/file_purpose`, so a new evidence type needs no client release (docs/API_CONTRACTS.md §4.5).

purposeId.description: The `file_purpose` dictionary item this file was uploaded against.

downloadPath.description: Path to fetch the bytes from **this** API. There is no direct storage URL and there never will be: the underlying link carries a bot token and expires within the hour, and §11.1 forbids permanently public links.

status.description: Overall service state. `degraded` means the API is serving but at least one dependency is unhealthy.

timestamp.description: When this response was produced. ISO-8601 with an explicit numeric offset, never `Z` (docs/API_CONTRACTS.md §2).
